arxiv-1712-07764.title: Wave function representation of probability distributions
arxiv-1712-07764.creator: Madeleine B. Thompson
arxiv-1712-07764.description: Abstract Orthogonal decomposition of the square root of a probability density function in the Hermite basis is a useful low-dimensional parameterization of continuous probability distributions over the reals. This representation is formally similar to the representation of quantum mechanical states as wave functions, whose squared modulus is a probability density.

arxiv-1907-01744.title: Region-Manipulated Fusion Networks for Pancreatitis Recognition
arxiv-1907-01744.creator: Jian Wang, Xiaoyao Li, Xiangbo Shu, Weiqin Li
arxiv-1907-01744.description: Abstract This work first attempts to automatically recognize pancreatitis on CT scan images. However, different form the traditional object recognition, such pancreatitis recognition is challenging due to the fine-grained and non-rigid appearance variability of the local diseased regions. To this end, we propose a customized Region-Manipulated Fusion Networks (RMFN) to capture the key characteristics of local lesion for pancreatitis recognition.

arxiv-2106-02002.title: Factorials and powers, a minimality result
arxiv-2106-02002.creator: David E. Radford
arxiv-2106-02002.description: Abstract Let a > 1 a>1 . Then a n < n ! a^{n}<n! for some positive integer n n . We show that the smallest such n n is one of a pair of possibilities, or is one possibility, which we show how to calculate. There are three interesting numerical sequences which play a central role in our arguments.

arxiv-2106-09487.title: Synthesizing Modular Manipulators For Tasks With Time, Obstacle, And Torque Constraints
arxiv-2106-09487.creator: Thais Campos, Hadas Kress-Gazit
arxiv-2106-09487.description: Abstract Modular robots can be tailored to achieve specific tasks and rearranged to achieve previously infeasible ones. The challenge is choosing an appropriate design from a large search space. In this work, we describe a framework that automatically synthesizes the design and controls for a serial chain modular manipulator given a task description.

arxiv-2110-11119.title: On the Burgers dynamical system with an external force and its Koopman decomposition
arxiv-2110-11119.creator: Mikhael Balabane
arxiv-2110-11119.description: Abstract We prove that the Burgers flow with a steady external forcing has a unique steady state which is a sink. Although this flow cannot be linearized through Cole-Hopf transforms, we prove that it has a convergent Koopman Modes decomposition. This gives an asymptotic formula for solutions of the Burgers equation with an external force.

arxiv-2308-00769.title: Unified unconditional regression for multivariate quantiles, M-quantiles and expectiles
arxiv-2308-00769.creator: Luca Merlo Department of Human Sciences, European University of Rome and Lea Petrella MEMOTEF Department, Sapienza University of Rome and Nicola Salvati Department of Economics and Management, University of Pisa and Nikos Tzavidis Department of Social Statistics and Demography, Southampton Statistic
arxiv-2308-00769.description: Abstract In this paper, we develop a unified regression approach to model unconditional quantiles, M-quantiles and expectiles of multivariate dependent variables exploiting the multidimensional Huber’s function. To assess the impact of changes in the covariates across the entire unconditional distribution of the responses, we extend the work of Firpo et al.

arxiv-2310-17050.title: Exploring Question Decomposition for Zero-Shot VQA
arxiv-2310-17050.creator: Zaid Khan, Vijay Kumar BG, Samuel Schulter, Manmohan Chandraker, Yun Fu
arxiv-2310-17050.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zaid Khan, Vijay Kumar BG, Samuel Schulter, Manmohan Chandraker, Yun Fu. Visual question answering (VQA) has traditionally been treated as a single-step task where each question receives the same amount of effort, unlike natural human question-answering strategies. We explore a question decomposition strategy for VQA to overcome this limitation. We probe the ability of recently developed large vision-language models to use human-written decompositions and produce their own decompositions of visual questions, finding they are capable of learning both tasks from demonstrations alone.

arxiv-2311-05746.title: Bridging the Digital Divide: Performance Variation across Socio-Economic Factors in Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2311-05746.creator: Joan Nwatu Oana Ignat Rada MihalceaUniversity of Michigan - Ann Arbor, USA{ jnwatu, oignat, mihalcea } @umich.edu
arxiv-2311-05746.description: Abstract Despite the impressive performance of current AI models reported across various tasks, performance reports often do not include evaluations of how these models perform on the specific groups that will be impacted by these technologies. Among the minority groups under-represented in AI, data from low-income households are often overlooked in data collection and model evaluation.

arxiv-2407-02679.title: Enhancing Scalability of Optimal Kron-based Reduction of Networks (Opti-KRON) via Decomposition with Community Detection Thanks: This work was supported by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy under the Enabling Place-Based Renewable Power Generation using
arxiv-2407-02679.creator: Omid Mokhtari, Samuel Chevalier, Mads R. Almassalkhi
arxiv-2407-02679.description: Abstract Electrical networks contain thousands of interconnected nodes and edges, which leads to computational challenges in some power system studies. To address these challenges, we contend that network reductions can serve as a framework to enable scalable computing in power systems.

arxiv-2510-24090.title: Tritiated methane reduction in the PandaX-4T experiment via purge and cryogenic distillation processes Journal: NUCL INSTRUM METH A
arxiv-2510-24090.creator: Shuaijie Li, Zhou Wang, Xiangyi Cui, Li Zhao, Yonglin Ju, Wenbo Ma, Yingjie Fan, Jianglai Liu, Liqiang Liu, Kai Kang
arxiv-2510-24090.description: Abstract Tritium from tritiated methane (CH 3 T) calibration is a significant impurity that restricts the sensitivity of the PandaX-4T dark matter detection experiment in the low-energy region. The CH 3 T removal is essential for PandaX-4T and other liquid xenon dark matter direct detection experiments, as CH 3 T serves as a critical component for low-energy calibration.

arxiv-2510-27565.title: CodeAlignBench : Assessing Code Generation Models on Developer-Preferred Code Adjustments
arxiv-2510-27565.creator: Forough Mehralian, Ryan Shar, James R. Rae & Alireza Hashemi
arxiv-2510-27565.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Forough Mehralian, Ryan Shar, James R. Rae & Alireza Hashemi. As large language models become increasingly capable of generating code, evaluating their performance remains a complex and evolving challenge. Existing benchmarks primarily focus on functional correctness, overlooking the diversity of real-world coding tasks and developer expectations. To this end, we introduce a multi-language benchmark that evaluates LLM instruction-following capabilities and is extensible to operate on any set of standalone coding problems.

arxiv-2511-05357.title: Diffusion-Based Electromagnetic Inverse Design of Scattering Structured Media
arxiv-2511-05357.creator: Mikhail Tsukerman, Konstantin Grotov, Pavel Ginzburg
arxiv-2511-05357.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mikhail Tsukerman, Konstantin Grotov, Pavel Ginzburg. We present a conditional diffusion model for electromagnetic inverse design that generates structured media geometries directly from target differential scattering cross-section profiles, bypassing expensive iterative optimization. Our 1D U-Net architecture with Feature-wise Linear Modulation learns to map desired angular scattering patterns to 2 × 2 2\times 2 dielectric sphere structure, naturally handling the non-uniqueness of inverse problems by sampling diverse valid designs.

arxiv-2511-16924.title: CBMA: Improving Conformal Prediction through Bayesian Model Averaging
arxiv-2511-16924.creator: Pankaj Bhagwat, Linglong Kong, Bei Jiang
arxiv-2511-16924.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pankaj Bhagwat, Linglong Kong, Bei Jiang. Conformal prediction has emerged as a popular technique for facilitating valid predictive inference across a spectrum of machine learning models, under minimal assumption of exchangeability. Recently, Hoff (2023) showed that full conformal Bayes provides the most efficient prediction sets (smallest by expected volume) among all prediction sets that are valid at the ( 1 − α ) (1-\alpha) level if the model is correctly specified.

arxiv-2601-10445.title: Modeling mental health trajectories during the COVID-19 pandemic using UK-wide data in the presence of sociodemographic variables
arxiv-2601-10445.creator: Glenna Nightingale, Karthik Mohan, Eloi Ribe, Valentin Popov, Shakes Wang, Clara Calia, Luciana Brondi, Sohan Seth
arxiv-2601-10445.description: Abstract Background: The negative effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on the mental health and well-being of populations are an important public health issue. Although several studies have reported on these effects in the UK, less is known about temporal trends and how different demographic groups were affected.

pmc-10695388.title: A disease associated mutant reveals how Ltv1 orchestrates RP assembly and rRNA folding of the small ribosomal subunit head
pmc-10695388.creator: Ebba K. Blomqvist, Haina Huang, Katrin Karbstein, Gregory P. Copenhaver, Anita K. Hopper, Gregory P. Copenhaver, Anita K. Hopper, Gregory P. Copenhaver, Anita K. Hopper
pmc-10695388.description: Ribosomes are complex macromolecules assembled from 4 rRNAs and 79 ribosomal proteins (RPs). Their assembly is organized in a highly hierarchical manner, which is thought to avoid dead-end pathways, thereby enabling efficient assembly of ribosomes in the large quantities needed for healthy cellular growth. Moreover, hierarchical assembly also can help ensure that each RP is included in the mature ribosome.

pmc-12540712.title: And-1 coordinates with polymerase δ to regulate nucleotide excision repair and UVB-induced skin tumorigenesis
pmc-12540712.creator: Shuyan Zhou, Yi Zhang, Zongzhu Li, Zhuqing Li, Patricia S Latham, Yunxiao Meng, Wen Chen, Penghua Yang, Chunyan Hou, Junfeng Ma, Wenge Zhu
pmc-12540712.description: The nucleotide excision repair (NER) pathway is the primary mechanism for removing UVB-induced photoproducts in mammals. While early steps of NER are well defined, the later step of gap-filling DNA synthesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we report And-1, a DNA replication and repair factor, as a critical regulator of this process.

pmc-12660768.title: A unified AI-driven framework for quantum-secured 6G THz networks with intelligent reflecting surfaces and federated edge learning
pmc-12660768.creator: C G Balaji, S Menaka, G Rajeswari, Sivaram Ponnusamy
pmc-12660768.description: The main contribution of this manuscript is an innovative framework for integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) in 6G wireless systems. With increased complexity, including bursty traffic, network complexity, and dynamic variability, there is a need for intelligence. This study develops and validates an AI-driven approach that enhances network performance through quantum communication decoding, beamforming, and decentralized edge processing.

pmc-13513043.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objective: In the multifactorial etiology of asthma, environmental factors, including sun exposure, measured either by sunshine hours (SHs) or global solar surface irradiance (GSSI), are critical. The objective of this study is to estimate the association between sun exposure and the prevalence of asthma in Spanish schoolchildren (6–7 years old) and adolescents (13–14 years old) from six geographic centers in Spain (A Coruña, Bilbao, Cantabria, Cartagena, Pamplona and Salamanca) included in the Global Asthma Network (GAN) study during 2016–2019.

pmc-13525947.title: Preliminary miRNA profiling of plasma from patients infected with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants
pmc-13525947.creator: Ivana Baranova, Dana Dvorska, Andrea Kapinova, Dusan Brany, Marek Samec, Eva Baranovicova, Veronika Holubekova, Zuzana Kolkova, Maria Skerenova, Dusan Loderer, Elena Novakova, Erika Halasova, Peter Liptak, Peter Banovcin, Anna Bobcakova, Robert Rosolanka, Zuzana Dankova
pmc-13525947.description: BackgroundEpigenetic regulation can play a dual role in viral infection, acting as part of the host defense, while being hijacked to control viral latency, replication, and persistence. During the COVID-19 pandemic, substantial evidence indicated that different SARS-CoV-2 variants may lead to distinct outcomes by affecting different molecular pathways, including epigenetic mechanisms.

pmc-13613778.title: Equine neuroborreliosis in Scandinavia: cerebrospinal fluid PCR confirmation and successful treatment in a mare
pmc-13613778.creator: Sofia Ruiz, Marianne Øverlie, Amanda Bergren, Ingunn Risnes Hellings
pmc-13613778.description: BackgroundLyme borreliosis (LB), caused by Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato, is an emerging concern in human medicine, and is a controversial topic in equine medicine. Neuroborreliosis (NB), a neurologic manifestation of LB, remains challenging to diagnose due to nonspecific clinical signs and the lack of definitive diagnostic methods. This report describes the first documented case of equine NB in Scandinavia.
